findings.title: Tag namespace guard is lexical-prefix only; does not reject path separators or '..'
findings.detail: Line 347 enforces args.tag.startswith('t3r_gate0'), so a tag like 't3r_gate0/../X' passes the guard while violating the stated namespace intent (the guard's own message at line 348 says 'tag must stay inside the t3r_gate0* namespace'). Verified inert in the current state: g0b_d420 contains no subdirectories (ls confirmed files only), so any traversal path has a nonexistent intermediate component and POSIX resolution returns ENOENT — scratchpad test confirmed both Path.exists() -> False AND write_text() -> FileNotFoundError, so no frozen file (t3_grasp*, t3_jaw_audit*, existing t3r_*) can be reached or clobbered; additionally the six-path preexisting guard (line 356) blocks any same-name overwrite of an existing file. Residual risk is only future-state (if a t3r_gate0*-named subdirectory ever appears) and the preregistered run uses the default tag. Defense-in-depth gap, not a reachable hazard.
findings.repair: Add `if args.tag != Path(args.tag).name or '..' in args.tag: raise ValueError(...)` next to the prefix check to make the namespace guard structural rather than lexical.

findings.title: Two exit-path classes emit no G0B_T3R_GATE0_VERDICT stdout line
findings.detail: (1) The tag-guard violation raises bare ValueError (line 348) -> traceback, exit code 1, no verdict line. (2) Any unhandled exception in the measurement phase (load_binary_stl ValueError at lines 204-209, FileNotFoundError from _sha256_file on a missing mesh at line 377, extract_usd_joint AttributeError/TypeError on a failed Usd.Stage.Open at lines 288-301) also exits without a verdict line. This weakens the 'stdout verdict in every exit path' ideal, but: it exactly matches the proven predecessor's behavior (g0b_t3_attempt3...audit.py lines 375-376 raise the same bare ValueError, and its measurement-phase RuntimeErrors also propagate — that script survived the 4-lens panel); all pre-line-500 exceptions are write-free so the tag is NOT burned; and post-write exceptions leave the results JSON (co-authority) carrying the verdict. Exit codes are documented non-authoritative (docstring lines 45-46, D424-③), so no wrong verdict can be read from these paths.
findings.repair: Wrap main() body in try/except that prints 'G0B_T3R_GATE0_VERDICT=GATE0_ABORT unhandled_exception=<repr>' before re-raising, or accept as precedent-consistent and note it in the session doc.

findings.title: argparse usage-error exit code 2 collides with the 'completed, non-PRESENT verdict' return 2
findings.detail: argparse exits with code 2 on unknown arguments (line 344-346), the same code returned at line 702 for a completed run whose verdict is not GATE0_SOURCE_PRESENT or whose rerun validation failed. Inert because the docstring (lines 45-46) explicitly declares exit code NOT a verdict channel per D424-③, and the argparse path writes nothing.
findings.repair: None required; optionally reserve a distinct code (e.g., 4) for completed-but-not-PRESENT if exit-code hygiene is ever wanted.

findings.title: Validation JSON retains default=str (D425-④ pattern) but is provably inert
findings.detail: Line 697 dumps the rerun-validation report with default=str — the exact serialization pattern D425-④ flagged as the string-boolean trap. Traced validate_rerun_artifact (roarm_rl/rerun_contract.py): every value is native str/int/bool/None/list/dict — subprocess text, int(returncode) (line 41), bool() casts (lines 43/244/259/325), and report['pass'] = not errors (line 351) is a native bool — so default=str can never fire and no 'True'/'False' strings can appear. The authority results JSON at line 581 correctly drops default entirely, and the collision cross-reference (lines 507-517) defensively float()-casts audit3 numerics with a comment citing D425-④. The consuming check at line 702 (validation.get('pass')) reads the in-memory native bool, not the file.
findings.repair: None required; optionally drop default=str for symmetry with the results dump.

positive_confirmations: (a) Complete write enumeration — exactly six filesystem writes, all under OUT_DIR=claudedocs/runtime_logs/grasp_track/g0b_d420 with the tag-prefixed names: {tag}_bands.csv (script line 500), {tag}_results.json (581), {tag}_timeline.rrd (rec.save sink at 598, finalized at context exit 662), {tag}_timeline.rbl (663), {tag}_rerun_validation.json (697), {tag}_inspection.png (written inside validate_rerun_artifact, rerun_contract.py lines 305-328, which itself REFUSES to overwrite an existing screenshot at lines 297-303; its mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) at 296 is inert since OUT_DIR exists). No other write call exists in the file. The preexisting-artifact guard at lines 356-359 covers ALL six paths. Tag prefix guard (347) plus dir listing (no existing t3r_gate0*-named files in g0b_d420; frozen t3r_* files are t3r_design_/t3r_selfbind_/t3r_tiebreak_) means no name collision with any frozen artifact is possible.

(a) No code path writes the STLs, the URDF, the attempt3 USD, t3_grasp*, t3_jaw_audit*, or existing t3r_* files: STLs via path.read_bytes() (203), URDF via ET.parse + read_text() (311, 338), attempt3 USD via sha-stream read (383-384) and Usd.Stage.Open (291), audit3 JSON via read_text() (507) — all read-only.

(b) D415-③ scope confirmed: grep over the whole file finds no Save/Export/SdfLayer/CreateAttribute/.Set(/DefinePrim/OverridePrim/Flatten/omni.kit API — the only 'omni'/'kit' hits are the extscache path string (57) and docstring text. pxr usage is Usd.Stage.Open + Get() reads only (extract_usd_joint, 288-301). No Kit launch; plain-python re-exec bootstrap (62-76) matches the 23rd proven pattern. Both attempt3 layer shas are pinned at GV1 (119-121, 383-385) before the stage is opened.

(c) Dead-asset rule verified by data flow: gripper_left_link.stl is sha-recorded (381-382) with an explicit '(recorded, NOT used)' stdout note (387) and results field "used": False (552), but load_binary_stl is only ever called on VIS_PINS entries (420) — the dead asset is never loaded, sampled, or transformed. Check direction correct: parse_urdf sets dead_asset_referenced = ('gripper_left_link.stl' in URDF text) (338); GV2 requires dead_ok = not referenced (408-409) — i.e. referenced must be False to pass. Ground truth confirmed: grep -c over roarm_m3.urdf returns 0 occurrences, and the file does exist in meshes/ so the sha record will populate.

(d) Results JSON (authority, dumped WITHOUT default at line 581) is numpy-TypeError-safe by full value trace: body_metrics returns only float()/int()/None (256-264) — feeds fixed (457), anchors (487-489); moving_peak float()-wrapped (481); coarse grid/l_vis list-comprehended through float() (572-573); gates bool()/float()-wrapped (564-567); sources are hexdigest strings/None/bool() (549-554); frames float()-wrapped (556-562); cross is float()/str (510-519); mesh_stats int()/float() (577-578); env strings (579). Scratchpad-verified type semantics: np.float64 IS a float subclass and serializes even if it leaked; np.float32/np.int64/np.bool_ would raise but none can reach the doc (every int is int()-cast, every bool is bool()-cast, np.allclose returns native bool). Frozen audit3 inputs verified directly: all 14 profile.assembly_max_depth_mm are native JSON floats (4.4576…), all 14 min_r_mm_in_rim_band are None — float() at 508 and 'is None' at 509 cannot crash.

(d/f) Write ORDER is safe: results JSON (581) is written BEFORE the RRD block (597) — a dump-time TypeError could strand at most the bands CSV, and per the trace cannot occur; the verdict is therefore on disk in the authority JSON before any Rerun artifact exists.

(e) Verdict stdout line present on every DESIGNED exit path: bootstrap abort (68), preexisting-artifact abort (358), rerun-version abort (363), GV1/GV2/GV3/GV4 aborts (389/413/429/452), and the completion path (701) which prints the verdict unconditionally before the exit-code computation (702). A mid-RRD exception still finalizes the sink via RecordingStream context exit (597-662) and leaves the verdict in the already-written results JSON. validate_rerun_artifact cannot realistically raise (its _run wraps every subprocess call in try/except returning ok=False, contract lines 29-52; screenshot-exists is handled as a report error, 297-303), so the validation JSON write (697) and verdict print (698-701) are reached even when validation FAILS — failure surfaces as pass=False and exit 2, not a strand.

findings.title: 3D pose at the decision-critical peak angle is not guaranteed to be in the RRD
findings.detail: gate0/gripper_vis is logged only at the six preregistered ANCHOR_Q5_DEG angles (line 145: 88.31/60/45/24/5/0, mapped at line 608, gated at line 616). The moving-jaw verdict is decided by the PEAK of L_vis over the sweep (coarse argmax k at line 471, refined at lines 474-481), and Gate-0 is explicitly preregistered 'before any mesh was profiled' (line 22), so there is no a-priori guarantee the peak falls at or near an anchor. If the visual-mesh peak lands mid-range (e.g. ~70 deg), the RRD can never display the jaw at the decision-critical configuration — the D341 requirement that the RRD contain 'the actual decision subject' and a decision-time diagnostic snapshot is then only satisfiable via the scalar curve, not the 3D geometry, and the human visual inspection (D425-①) cannot see WHERE the deepest geometry is at the deciding angle. The predecessor logged the jaw pose at every timeline index, so this is a coverage regression introduced by anchor-only decimation (which goes beyond the adopted 28th accel-⑤ 1/16 point-stride default). Verdict itself is unaffected (stdout+JSON authority), hence MAJOR not FATAL.
findings.repair: Guarantee the coarse-peak pose is logged: before the loop build `anchor_ids = set(anchor_idx.values()) | {k}` (k, the coarse argmax index from line 471, is in scope) and change line 616 to `if i in anchor_ids:`. No new entity, contract unchanged, size cost ~0.43 MB (one more 35,926-pt cloud). Optionally mention the peak-index cloud in the summary_md legend.

findings.title: Unguarded observability block can suppress the stdout verdict channel and burn the single shot
findings.detail: The declared authority is 'stdout verdict line + results JSON' (line 45-46), but the final G0B_T3R_GATE0_VERDICT print (line 701) sits AFTER the entire Rerun+validation block (lines 583-698). Any uncaught exception in that block (imports at 584-585, rec/log calls, blueprint.save at 663, or an internal error inside validate_rerun_artifact — the validator guards subprocess failures but not its own exceptions, and then validation JSON at line 697 is never written) kills one of the two authority channels even though the scientific result is complete on disk, and leaves partial artifacts (results JSON, bands CSV, RRD) that trigger the preexisting-artifact GATE0_ABORT (lines 356-359) on any re-run. D341 states visualization-contract failure must not override the scientific verdict. Probability is low (all API signatures and component names verified against 0.34.1 and the predecessor's passing run) and the pattern is inherited verbatim from the predecessor (lines 623-770), hence MINOR.
findings.repair: Wrap lines 583-698 in try/except; on exception record {'pass': False, 'errors': ['viz-layer exception: ...']} to validation_path and continue, so lines 699-702 always print the artifact line and the verdict line, and the exit code degrades to 2 via the existing `validation.get('pass')` term.

findings.title: Gates TextLog drops explicit pass text; INDETERMINATE is colored as ERROR
findings.detail: Line 623 logs `rr.TextLog(f"{name}", level=INFO if ok else ERROR)` — the predecessor logged `f"{name} pass={ok}"` (predecessor line 693). GV1-GV4 rows carry pass/fail only via level color (all necessarily True at this point since failures abort earlier, so low impact), but the G0_fixed_*/G0_moving_* rows use `ok = (state == "PASS")` (line 622), so a legitimate INDETERMINATE outcome renders at ERROR level in panel 3, visually indistinguishable by color from FAIL during the mandated visual inspection; only the embedded state suffix in the name disambiguates.
findings.repair: Log `rr.TextLog(f"{name} state_ok={ok}", ...)` (or per-row explicit state text) and consider TextLogLevel.WARN for INDETERMINATE rows so the three-way outcome is distinguishable by level, matching the tri-state gate design.

findings.title: Refined 0.02-deg sweep is not logged to the plots; only the 0.25-deg coarse curve is
findings.detail: The refined peak (lines 474-481) appears in summary_md and results JSON, but plots/l_vis_moving_mm (line 613) contains only the 354-point coarse curve, so the Rerun timeseries under-represents the reported peak by up to one coarse step. Acceptable for a presence gate with 0.5 mm indeterminate half-width and consistent with 'authority = stdout + results JSON' (line 640), but worth knowing during visual inspection that the plotted maximum may sit slightly below the quoted peak value.
findings.repair: No change required; optionally log a static or single-point plots/l_vis_peak_mm scalar at the coarse-peak index (would require adding it to expected_entities and components) or note the coarse-vs-refined delta in summary_md.

lenses.lens: LENS 4 — Rerun / D341 observability contract (entity/timeline/component contracts, anchor logging, RRD size vs screenshot race, blueprint, summary accuracy, validator call)
positive_confirmations: (a) Entity contract is exactly bidirectional: the 12 logged entities (lines 599-642) equal expected_entities/exact_entity_paths (lines 665-669); every component name in the mapping (lines 670-683) is empirically proven against rerun 0.34.1 — the predecessor's passing validation JSON (t3_jaw_audit3_rerun_validation.json) observed Points3D:{positions,colors,radii}, LineStrips3D:{strips,colors,radii}, Scalars:scalars, TextLog:{text,level}, TextDocument:{text,media_type} (subset check covers the extra media_type), and system entities (/__properties, /viewport, /container/*, /view/*, panels) are filtered by _is_system_entity (rerun_contract.py:105-111).

(b) Timeline contract uses SET semantics, not order: exact_timeline_names is converted to a set (rerun_contract.py:148-152) and compared as sets (rerun_contract.py:264-266), so ['blueprint','log_time','sweep_index'] (line 688) is correct; the 'blueprint' index name is empirically confirmed in the predecessor's observed list ['band_index','blueprint','log_time']; statics create no index entries; the gates TextLog is stamped on sweep_index=0 via reset_time+set_time (lines 619-620) — the audit3 lesson is preserved.

(c) Anchor logging verified numerically in scratch: grid length 354 (Q5_OPEN + arange(88.0,-0.001,-0.25)); anchors map to indices {88.3100:0, 60:113, 45:173, 24:257, 5:333, 0:353}, every mapped grid value is an EXACT angle match (no off-by-one), all six indices distinct, and index 0 is covered, so latest-at-or-before shows a gripper pose at every cursor position; `i in anchor_idx.values()` membership is correct.

(d) RRD size estimate from the actual pinned STLs: link5 2,266,503 samples -> 141,656 static points (~1.7 MB) + 6 anchor clouds x 35,926 points (~2.6 MB) + 4x354=1,416 scalar rows + rings/TextLog => ~4.5-6.5 MB total, the same class as the predecessor's proven 4.3 MB RRD that produced a clean 5.2 MB screenshot after the D425-② 1/16 fix; VIEW_STRIDE=16 is applied at BOTH heavy sites (line 599 link5_vis, line 618 gripper_vis) — no undecimated heavy log exists.

(e) Blueprint: all five views reference only logged entities; TimeSeriesView contents syntax is byte-pattern-identical to the proven predecessor (pred. lines 708-725); blueprint.save(app_id, rbl_path) runs AFTER the RecordingStream context exits (line 663 vs with-block end at 662), matching predecessor order; screenshot_window_size '2400x1400' matches the validator arg; the final timeline cursor (index 353) carries a fresh q5=0 anchor pose, so the headless PNG renders current geometry, and the L_MIN rings (r=12.5/20 mm at z=-5.5 mm) are visible within the ~170 mm auto-fit scene extent.

(f) summary_md audited number-by-number: shas dict keys ('link5.stl','gripper_link.stl') correct; L_vis/peak/gate constants all from computed variables; the collision cross-ref values verified against the frozen t3_jaw_audit3_results.json (14 profile rows, all assembly_max_depth_mm floats — max 4.4576 mm matching the D425 plug depth 4.458, min_r_mm_in_rim_band None at 14/14 angles, so line 507-509 cannot crash and 'rim band empty 14/14' is accurate); the color legend matches actual RGB values (grey 150/150/160, blue 70/130/230, green 40/200/80, orange 230/120/40, red 235/60/60); 'view decimated 1/16' matches VIEW_STRIDE.

(g) validate_rerun_artifact call (lines 684-696) matches the signature (rerun_contract.py:114-130) argument-for-argument; timeout_s=180 is per-subprocess and proven adequate by the predecessor run; SDK 0.34.1 and CLI 0.34.1 verified live in the isaaclab env, and RecordingStream(__init__ with recording_id/make_default/send_properties), save(path, write_footer=True), set_time(timeline, sequence=), flush(timeout_sec=), send_blueprint(make_active=, make_default=), and Blueprint.save(application_id, path) all verified via inspect.signature.

No frozen-artifact risk from the observability layer: the tag guard forces the t3r_gate0* namespace (lines 347-348), all six output paths are pre-checked for nonexistence (lines 356-359), the validator refuses to overwrite an existing screenshot (rerun_contract.py:298-303), and no t3r_gate0* artifact currently exists in g0b_d420.

D341 ordering respected: rec.save() attaches the file sink as the first call inside the context before any log (line 598), and the recording is finalized by context exit (line 662) before blueprint export, validation, hashing, or the artifact gate run.

findings.title: Verdict-driving moving-jaw peak pose has no discriminator metrics (no r_at_l_vis, no annulus/footprint split, no bands rows at peak q5)
findings.detail: moving_peak (line 481) records only {q5_deg, l_vis_mm}. body_metrics (r_at_l_vis_mm, max_depth_in_footprint_mm, max_depth_in_wall_annulus_mm, rim-band stats) are computed only at the 6 preset ANCHOR_Q5_DEG poses (lines 486-493), and band_rows only at those same anchors (lines 495-499). If the refined peak falls between anchors (e.g. q5=33°), the exact pose that determines the moving-jaw PASS/FAIL/INDETERMINATE has no radial localization in any artifact. This directly weakens lens questions (a) and (b): a PASS could ride on a point whose radius/azimuth is unreported, and the arm design cannot fully audit the peak without re-running a single-shot script. The fixed jaw does report r_at_l_vis (line 459), making the moving-jaw omission an asymmetry, not a design choice.
findings.repair: Legal preregistration edit (before the run): at the refined peak q5, compute d,r = depth_r_mm(transform_pts(gripper_T_l5(joint, peak_q5), grip_pts_g)) and store body_metrics(d,r) as moving_gripper_link.peak_metrics in results JSON; also append band_rows('gripper_link', f'peak_{q5:.4f}', d, r) to the bands CSV; additionally record the peak point's azimuth atan2(y,x) and body-local coordinates for both bodies' peaks so non-finger structure is localizable post-hoc without re-running.

findings.title: r<=30mm finger window admits non-finger axial structure (plug-analog central boss) and open-angle-only peaks — verdict-class false PASS possible
findings.detail: l_vis_mm (lines 245-247) takes max depth over ALL points with r<=FINGER_WINDOW_R_MM=30, with no lower radial bound and no azimuth/angle qualification. Two false-PASS vectors: (1) radial — a central camera-boss/plug-analog structure near the tool axis (the same visual-mesh family that produced collision part_029/030 at r≈11.77mm, D425) deeper than 6.0mm would yield GATE0_SOURCE_PRESENT with zero authorable finger geometry in the wall-contact band (12.5-20mm); (2) angular — for the moving jaw, max-over-sweep counts a peak reached only at wide-open q5 (e.g. heel structure rotating down at 88°), unusable at grasp-relevant closing angles (~24-45°). Mitigations already present but report-only and not preregistered as interpretation rules: r_at_l_vis (fixed jaw only, see MAJOR-1 for moving gap), footprint-vs-annulus split, peak q5 and full coarse l_vis(q5) curve in JSON. The ABSENT direction is sound (absence under max-over-sweep implies absence everywhere), so the hole is one-sided toward false PRESENT. Honest mitigation: the frozen collision cook (derived from these visual meshes) bounds central structure at ~4.458mm < 5.0 FAIL threshold, but not trusting the collision layer to bound the visual layer is this gate's entire premise.
findings.repair: Do NOT change the gate (r<=30 max-over-sweep stays as preregistered). Add preregistered secondary REPORT metrics per body: (i) l_vis restricted to the wall annulus 12.5<=r<=20 ('l_vis_wall_mm'), (ii) azimuth at peak, (iii) for the moving jaw, l_vis restricted to grasp-relevant q5 in [0,45] ('l_vis_grasp_range_mm'); plus a written interpretation rule in results JSON: a PRESENT verdict with r_at_l_vis < 12.5mm or peak only at q5 > 60° requires explicit manual review before Arm-F/D authoring proceeds.

findings.title: Report-only cross-ref and bands CSV sit on the verdict critical path; stdout verdict line emitted only after the full rerun+validation chain
findings.detail: Execution order: bands CSV written (lines 500-503) -> audit3 cross-ref read (507-509, declared 'report-only') -> verdict computed (525-532) -> results JSON written (581) -> rerun recording/validation (583-697) -> stdout G0B_T3R_GATE0_VERDICT line (701). Consequences: (1) any exception in the report-only cross-ref (e.g. audit3 file moved) aborts before the preregistered verdict exists anywhere, with the bands CSV already on disk blocking a same-tag re-run via the preexisting-artifact guard (356-359); (2) any exception in the RecordingStream block, blueprint.save (663), or validate_rerun_artifact (684) suppresses the stdout verdict line even though results JSON holds the verdict — half of the declared dual authority channel ('stdout verdict line + results json', docstring line 45) dies with a viz failure. I verified the frozen audit3 JSON has all consumed fields (14/14 entries, float/None types), so residual crash probability is low — hence MINOR, not MAJOR. Recovery exists via a new tag inside the t3r_gate0* namespace.
findings.repair: Print the G0B_T3R_GATE0_VERDICT line immediately after results_path.write_text (line 581) in addition to the final print; move the audit3 cross-ref read into a try/except that degrades to a recorded 'cross_ref_error' field instead of crashing (it is report-only by declaration, make it report-only by construction); optionally write the bands CSV after the results JSON.

findings.title: -Infinity can enter results JSON (invalid strict JSON) when a sweep pose has no points inside the finger window
findings.detail: l_vis_mm returns -math.inf when no sampled point satisfies r<=30 at a given q5 (line 247). For the moving jaw at wide-open angles the whole body may leave the window, so coarse_l_vis_mm (line 573) and anchor l_vis values could contain float('-inf'). json.dumps serializes this as -Infinity (scratch-verified), which Python re-loads but strict parsers (jq, other languages, some validators) reject — degrading the frozen evidence artifact's machine-readability. tri_state(-inf)=FAIL is semantically correct and unaffected.
findings.repair: Sanitize at serialization: map non-finite floats to None (with a documented convention, e.g. 'null = no geometry inside finger window at this pose') in coarse_l_vis_mm, anchors, and fixed/moving metrics before json.dumps; alternatively pass a custom encoder. Keep the -inf semantics internal to tri_state.

findings.title: Sweep discretization error bound undocumented; refine polishes only the single best coarse local maximum
findings.detail: Coarse sweep is 0.25 deg (line 465) and refine covers only ±1.0 deg around the single argmax (lines 471-474). If l_vis(q5) is multimodal with two near-equal maxima more than 1 deg apart, the true global peak can be missed by up to ~0.2-0.4mm (point radius from joint axis ~0.1m x 0.125 deg half-step), a one-sided underestimate comparable to the 0.5mm indeterminate half-width. Surface sampling at 0.5mm pitch adds a further one-sided underestimate only where the constrained max lies on the r=30 window boundary mid-triangle (unconstrained triangle max is always at a vertex — scratch-verified the linearity argument, vertices are all included at line 218). Combined worst case cannot flip PASS<->FAIL (needs >1.0mm) but can shift a boundary value across one tri-state edge in the conservative (toward FAIL/INDET) direction. No error budget is stated in the results JSON.
findings.repair: Preregister the numeric error bound in results_doc.gates (e.g. 'sweep_depth_error_bound_mm' with the radius x half-step derivation), and refine around the top-3 distinct coarse local maxima instead of only argmax (cheap: ~300 extra pose evaluations).

findings.title: L_MIN anchored to m=5.5 while effectuated D426 G-e margin floor is 4.5mm — 1.0mm gap exceeds the 0.5mm indeterminate half-width and is not preregistered as a rationale
findings.detail: The gate derivation (lines 22-27, 546) uses m=5.5mm (attempt2 precedent) giving L in (5.5,17.5], matching 24th doc §4-1 verbatim. But the effectuated tie-break guard G-e (D426-② / DECISIONS.md D426) fixes the F-fallback invariant at margin >= +4.5mm (x <= L-4.5). Under m=4.5 the viable range is L in (4.5,16.5]: a measured L_vis in [4.5,5.0) would be classed FAIL -> GATE0_SOURCE_ABSENT (triggering the drastic user-requery branch) even though a margin-4.5 design could in principle achieve x in (0,0.5]. Defensible — a <=0.5mm bite is not a usable pinch and the script matches its design authority — but the discrepancy between the two authored margins is nowhere acknowledged, inviting a post-hoc dispute of an ABSENT verdict measured in that 1.0mm strip.
findings.repair: Add one sentence to the derivation string / header: L_MIN is anchored to the attempt2 margin precedent m=5.5 (not the G-e floor 4.5) because grip depths x<=1.0mm are not operationally usable; note that L_vis in [4.5,5.0) still verdicts FAIL by preregistration. Purely documentary — no gate change.

findings.title: Recommended authoring band L=9.5-13.5mm (24th §4-1) not recorded in gate_contract
findings.detail: A source can PASS at 6.1mm yet be unusable for the recommended band. The raw peaks + full coarse l_vis(q5) curve + bands CSV do allow detecting this without re-running (lens (a) answer is yes), but the interpreter must fetch 9.5-13.5 from the 24th session doc; the results JSON is not self-contained on this point.
findings.repair: Add 'recommended_L_band_mm': [9.5, 13.5] (24th §4-1) to gate_contract, and optionally a derived boolean per body 'peak_reaches_recommended_band'.

findings.title: Per-body INDETERMINATE states logged to Rerun at TextLogLevel.ERROR
findings.detail: Lines 621-623 mark gate events ERROR whenever state != PASS, so G0_fixed_INDETERMINATE / G0_moving_INDETERMINATE render as errors in the viewer, conflating a preregistered three-valued outcome with a failure during visual inspection (D341 inspection is mandatory, so the coloring will be seen).
findings.repair: Use TextLogLevel.WARN for INDETERMINATE and ERROR only for FAIL.

lenses.lens: LENS 3 — PREREGISTRATION / METHODOLOGY (Gate-0 derivation, false-PASS/false-FAIL, tri-state semantics, verdict mapping, failability, cross-reference integrity, claim-layer discipline)
positive_confirmations: (d) Tri-state boundaries scratch-verified numerically: l_vis=6.0 -> INDETERMINATE, 5.0 -> INDETERMINATE, 6.0000001 -> PASS, 4.9999999 -> FAIL, -inf -> FAIL (lines 279-284). Strict inequalities exactly implement '|L_vis-5.5| <= 0.5 => indeterminate' symmetrically; header text (line 35) matches code.

(e) Verdict mapping (lines 526-532) verified: PRESENT requires BOTH bodies PASS; any FAIL -> ABSENT; one PASS + one INDETERMINATE -> GATE0_INDETERMINATE. PRESENT with an INDETERMINATE body is structurally impossible. Matches the 24th doc §4 row-2 both-bodies requirement (F축 = 양쪽 body, body별 각각 게이트).

(f) GATE0_SOURCE_ABSENT is genuinely reachable and plausible: any body with measured l_vis < 5.0mm (e.g. visual meshes mirroring the frozen collision reality — moving jaw 3.956mm / plug 4.458mm) produces FAIL -> ABSENT. D368's motivation makes ABSENT a live outcome; session-progress (failable experiment) rule satisfied.

(g) audit3 consumption dodges the D425-③ string-boolean trap: only profile[].assembly_max_depth_mm (verified float in 14/14 entries) and min_r_mm_in_rim_band (verified float/None) are consumed; the actual trap field gates.ANGLE_INV (verified to be string 'True' in the frozen JSON) is never read. 'Plug-dominated' framing verified accurate: assembly_max_depth_mm constant 4.457623mm across all 14 angles == D425 plug depth; rim band None 14/14.

(h) Claim-layer discipline holds everywhere I checked: docstring lines 8-11, results 'layer' field (539-540), summary_md (626), stdout lines — all confine claims to the authoring-source layer with explicit 'not physics / not real-gripper / not visual-matches-real (T4 layer)' disclaimers. The SOURCE_ABSENT branch text (lines 41-43) matches D426-① verbatim semantics (C extinct, hand-authoring or stop-and-reconsult only, user re-query mandatory, script only reports). D426-④ (B/F/D incremental, D415-③ untouched) and D426-⑤ (Gate-0 first, gripper_left_link.stl forbidden) citations verified against DECISIONS.md D426 full text.

(a) Gate derivation string (lines 22-27, 546) matches 24th §4-1 verbatim (x=L-m, m=5.5, x in (0,12] => L in (5.5,17.5]); using the lower bound as a presence/necessity gate is sound preregistration for a SOURCE audit (authoring sub-selects from what exists). Peak values, the full coarse l_vis(q5) curve, and the bands CSV do allow detecting a shallow-PASS-below-recommended-band case without re-running (gaps: MAJOR-1, INFO recommended-band).

(c) Per-q5 window masking with max-over-sweep is the correct NECESSITY quantifier against false-FAIL: usable finger geometry must enter r<=30 at grasp-relevant angles (pinching the D29 cylinder wall at r≈14.5 requires window entry near closing); geometry that never enters the window at any q5 in [0, 88.31] cannot pinch. Sweep grid scratch-verified: 354 points covering exactly [0.0, 88.0] at 0.25° plus Q5_OPEN=88.3096; refine grid inclusive of both ends; the 88.0-88.31 gap is covered by the ±1.0° refine window from either end.

All four GV abort-gates pre-verified against ground truth so the single shot cannot be burned by a spurious GATE0_ABORT: STL sha pins match (gripper_link.stl 7946a374…, link5.stl 1d63f374… in urdf/meshes/), both files are valid binary STL (13698 / 14092 triangles, size == 84+50n), URDF wiring exactly matches GV2 (single visual per link, origin '0 0 0'/'0 0 0', scale '0.001 0.001 0.001', filenames 'meshes/<f>.stl'), joint upper limit 1.571 rad = 90.0002° passes the 0.1° tolerance, lower = 0, axis '0.0 0.0 1.0', TCP origin exactly '0 0 0.115428' (== TCP_LOCAL, atol 1e-9 passes), dead asset gripper_left_link.stl exists on disk but is genuinely absent from the URDF text (substring check passes), attempt3 USD root+physics shas match pins.

Environment pins verified: installed rerun-sdk == 0.34.1 == RERUN_VERSION, RERUN_CLI path exists, USD_LIBS extscache dir exists (bootstrap will not abort), roarm_kinematics.Tmat exists (roarm_kinematics.py:46, same import family as the proven 23rd predecessor). validate_rerun_artifact signature (rerun_contract.py:114-130) accepts every kwarg the script passes.

Frozen-artifact protection verified: preexisting-artifact refusal (lines 356-359) plus the tag namespace guard requiring 't3r_gate0' prefix (lines 347-348) make overwriting frozen t3_* / earlier t3r_* outputs impossible; all identity/wiring/units/frame aborts occur before any file is written.

View-frame sign consistency verified by algebra: mesh points (view_pts, lines 589-591) and reference rings (ring, lines 593-595) both map depth-positive (below TCP, +z in link5 frame) to view -z, so the L_MIN plane, cylinder reference, and mesh cloud are mutually consistent in the inspection scene. Rerun API usage (RecordingStream kwargs, set_time/reset_time, Scalars, TextLog, send_blueprint, blueprint.save) matches the panel-surviving 23rd predecessor line-for-line.

Reviewer discipline note: I deliberately did NOT profile the STL depth/geometry (only format, size, sha), so the preregistration blindness of the gated quantity L_vis is preserved — all proposed repairs above are data-blind and remain legal preregistration edits.

findings.title: Single-peak refine can understate a near-tie secondary maximum by up to ~0.2 mm
findings.detail: The sweep refines only around the single global coarse argmax (k=argmax(sweep_l), then ±1.0 deg at 0.02 deg). A secondary local maximum in a different coarse cell is sampled only at 0.25 deg resolution; with max point radius about the joint axis bounded by the gripper bbox diagonal (measured 90.8 mm), the coarse sample can undershoot that local peak by up to 90.8 mm x sin(0.125 deg) = 0.198 mm. So if two peaks are within ~0.2 mm of each other, the reported moving-jaw L_vis can understate the true sweep maximum by up to ~0.2 mm (understate-only; never overstates). This can flip PASS->INDETERMINATE or INDETERMINATE->FAIL only when the true L_vis lies within 0.2 mm of the 6.0/5.0 mm boundaries, and FAIL forces GATE0_SOURCE_ABSENT (costly branch). The refined cell itself has residual only 90.8 mm x sin(0.01 deg) = 0.016 mm.
findings.repair: Either refine around the top 2-3 distinct coarse local maxima (cells separated by >2*REFINE_HALF_DEG) and take the best refined value, or preregister the derived +0.2 mm one-sided angular-quantization bound in the results JSON gates block and session doc so a boundary-adjacent tri-state is interpreted with it.

findings.title: Empty finger-window pathology yields substantive FAIL verdict, -Infinity in authority JSON, and a None-format crash path
findings.detail: If no sampled point has r<=30 mm, l_vis_mm() returns -math.inf (line 247). Consequences: (1) tri_state(-inf) -> FAIL -> GATE0_SOURCE_ABSENT, i.e., a frame/window anomaly is classified as the scientific 'source absent' result instead of GATE0_ABORT; (2) json.dumps serializes -inf as '-Infinity' (allow_nan default), making the authority results JSON invalid strict JSON (line 581 has no default= and no finiteness guard); (3) for the fixed jaw, body_metrics r_at_l_vis_mm would be None and the f-string at line 459 ('{fixed['r_at_l_vis_mm']:.2f}') raises TypeError before any verdict line. Plausibility is very low (the moving-jaw hub sits at r~18.8 mm from the tool axis and the link5 barrel straddles the axis, so the window is structurally non-empty at every angle, and GV3 bbox gates unit errors), so this is a robustness/misclassification gap rather than an expected-path defect.
findings.repair: After computing fixed/moving metrics, add an abort guard: if not math.isfinite(l_vis) for either body (or window point count == 0), print GATE0_ABORT with reason empty_finger_window and return 3, before tri_state and before any artifact write.

findings.title: GV4 'urdf agreement gated' does not check the URDF joint <axis> element that the witness formula assumes
findings.detail: parse_urdf stores joint axis (line 332: joint.find('axis').get('xyz')) but GV4 (lines 438-447) never validates it; the witness compares T_o @ Rz(+theta), which silently assumes the URDF axis is +z. The USD side axis=='Z' IS checked, and today's URDF is verified '0.0 0.0 1.0' (roarm_m3.urdf:229), so the current run cannot produce a wrong verdict from this. But the URDF file is the only load-bearing input without a sha pin (it was already edited post-attempt3: gripper_link collision now points at gripper_link_collision_g2a.stl, roarm_m3.urdf:161), and a future axis edit would not trip the witness (T_o excludes the axis element), leaving the printed claim 'urdf agreement gated' stronger than the actual gate coverage in the evidence chain.
findings.repair: Add to gv4: [float(v) for v in urdf['joint_origin']['axis'].split()] == [0.0, 0.0, 1.0] (or np.allclose), so the +z assumption behind T_o @ Rz(+theta) is an explicit gate; optionally record the URDF file sha256 in sources for the evidence chain.

findings.title: Q5_OPEN comment value 88.3096 does not match degrees(1.5413)=88.30998; anchor keys will read '88.3100'
findings.detail: math.degrees(1.5413) = 88.30998496..., not 88.3096 as the inline comment states (line 128, inherited verbatim from the proven predecessor line 93). Effect is cosmetic only: the anchors dict key and CSV q5 label will be '88.3100', and logs print 88.31; all computation uses the exact float. Worth knowing so the session doc quotes 88.3100 rather than 88.3096 when citing anchor keys.
findings.repair: Fix the comment to 88.3100 (or leave as-is and quote anchor keys as 88.3100 in the session doc); no code change needed.

findings.title: l_vis conflates any near-axis structure with 'finger'; window-boundary sampling error up to ~0.24 mm in one edge case
findings.detail: Two preregistered-design caveats, both adequately mitigated: (1) any geometry with r<=30 mm reaching depth>6.0 mm counts as source-present, including a hypothetical central boss/camera feature that is not jaw material — mitigated because r_at_l_vis_mm, the bands CSV, and the mandatory D341 visual inspection expose where the deep point is; the collision plug analogue sits at 4.458 mm < 5.0 mm so it cannot cause a false PASS. (2) The max-depth-at-vertex exactness argument (depth is affine per triangle) breaks only when the deepest in-window point lies on a triangle whose deepest vertex is outside r=30 mm; then the sampled max can understate by up to ~0.24 mm (measured toy coverage bound at 0.5 mm pitch). Physically implausible for jaw tips near the axis, and understate-only.
findings.repair: No code change required. During the D341 inspection, explicitly confirm r_at_l_vis_mm is jaw material (not a central boss), and note the 0.24 mm window-boundary caveat in the session doc only if r_at_l_vis lands within ~1 mm of 30 mm.

findings.title: bands CSV is written before the cross-ref/results/RRD blocks; a late crash leaves a partial artifact set that blocks retry
findings.detail: Write order: bands CSV (line 500) -> audit3 cross-ref parse (507) -> results JSON (581) -> RRD/validation. An exception in the cross-ref or Rerun block would leave the CSV (and possibly results JSON) on disk, and a retry then hits the preexisting_artifacts abort (line 356-359), requiring manual cleanup under the frozen-output folder. Risk is low: I verified today that the audit3 JSON exists with native-float profile fields ('assembly_max_depth_mm' float 4.4576, 'min_r_mm_in_rim_band' None x14 — no D425-3 string trap on the consumed fields), validate_rerun_artifact's signature matches the call exactly, and isaaclab has rerun 0.34.1 + the pinned CLI. No frozen artifact can be corrupted (all writes go to new t3r_gate0_* names).
findings.repair: Optional: move the bands CSV write after the results JSON write (verdict authority lands first), or accept the risk given the verified inputs; if a partial set ever occurs, delete only the t3r_gate0_vismesh_* files under g0b_d420 before retrying.

positive_confirmations: (a) STL parser is byte-exact: replicated load_binary_stl vs an independent per-record struct.unpack('<12fH') loop on both pinned meshes — max|diff| = 0.0 over 13698 (gripper_link.stl) and 14092 (link5.stl) triangles; dropped row 0 confirmed to be the NORMAL (100% of stored normals align with recomputed face normals, cos>0.99); '<f4' explicit little-endian; 84-byte offset/50-byte stride/attribute-count-ignored all spec-correct; arr[:, :48].copy() re-aligns so .view('<f4') is safe (tested from a misaligned base buffer); size formula 84+50n is the decisive binary check and both files satisfy it; no NaN/inf vertices in either mesh; GV3 would also catch NaN via bbox comparison semantics.

(a) Both visual sha pins match on disk today (gripper_link.stl 7946a374..., link5.stl 1d63f374...), USD root a4be58e8... and physics 043a5d35... pins match, dead asset gripper_left_link.stl exists (recorded-only) and appears 0 times in the URDF text — GV1/GV2 dead-asset gates will pass as intended.

(b) sample_triangles barycentric grid (ii+jj)<=n covers the full closed triangle: all 3 vertices present, hypotenuse (u+v=1) sampled, measured max surface-to-nearest-sample distance 0.243 mm at 0.5 mm pitch on a 10 mm toy triangle; degenerate (zero-area) and 100mm x 0.01mm sliver triangles handled without crash; duplicates are harmless for max/min metrics. Key exactness: depth is an affine function of position, so the max over each triangle is attained at a vertex and all vertices are included — the l_vis max-depth measurement is exact (not pitch-limited) whenever the deepest vertex is inside the r-window.

(c) Tool-frame conventions are line-identical to the proven predecessor (depth=(z-0.115428)*1000 positive below TCP; r=hypot(x,y); view_pts z-flip and ring() use consistent -depth), and the positive-below-TCP sign is anchored by the frozen audit3 numbers (assembly_max_depth_mm = +4.4576 = the plug 4.458 mm below TCP from D425).

(d) The 3-angle joint witness is algebraically sufficient: each entry of T_o@Rz(th) - T0@Rz(th)@inv(T1) has the form a + b cos(th) + c sin(th), which has at most 2 zeros per period unless identically zero, so vanishing at {0, 45, 88.31} deg forces equality for ALL th. Measured worst-case tolerance amplification over the swept interval [0, 88.31] deg is 1.296x (13.2x only over the full circle, never reached), so witness<1e-5 bounds placement error <=1.3e-5 (~0.013 mm) at every sweep angle — negligible vs the 0.5 mm indeterminate half-width. The residual algebraic freedom (a common z-screw offset between USD and URDF body frames) cancels exactly because the applied map is verified equal to the URDF map T_o@Rz(th), which is by definition the correct placement for URDF-frame visual points (visual origin identity is gated by GV2). Tmat/rpy_R = Rz(yaw)Ry(pitch)Rx(roll) matches the URDF fixed-axis XYZ convention (roarm_kinematics.py:39-50). Even if the USD authored exact pi/2 vs URDF 1.5708 (3.7e-6 rad), the witness diff stays ~3.7e-6 < 1e-5, passing either way.

(e) Sweep coverage verified numerically: np.arange(88.0, -0.001, -0.25) yields exactly 353 values ending at exactly 0.0 (dyadic arithmetic, no fp drift), plus Q5_OPEN prepended = 354 angles, zero duplicates; refine windows clamp correctly at both ends, always contain the coarse-peak angle, include the exact Q5_OPEN endpoint without exceeding it (last=88.30998496, max<=Q5_OPEN), and refine@0 spans [0.0, 1.0]; all six ANCHOR angles (88.31/60/45/24/5/0) coincide exactly with grid entries; band edges arange(-5, 30.5, 0.5) gives exactly 71 edges / 70 bands; argmax-on-plateau picks the first (open-most) index with no effect on the max value.

(f/g) Measured on the real meshes: 574,831 samples (gripper, 13.8 MB) + 2,266,503 samples (link5, 54.4 MB), sampling <0.1 s; one sweep step (transform+depth+r+mask+max over 575k points) = 8.3 ms, so 354 coarse + 51 refine + 6 anchors + 6 band passes complete in roughly 4-10 s — comfortably minutes-scale. GV3 extents gates pass with margin (gripper 77.9/25.2/39.4 mm; link5 46.5/35.5/120.6 mm, all inside (5, 400) mm). RRD payload at 1/16 view decimation is ~<10 MB, under the 27.9 MB size that raced the screenshot loader in D425. GV4 boundary values verified against the URDF: lower=0, upper=1.571 rad = 90.0117 deg passes the <0.1 deg gate; USD limits [0, 90] known from the 23rd run.

Environment preflight (no run consumed): isaaclab python has rerun 0.34.1 and numpy 1.26.0 (D326 pin intact), the pinned rerun CLI exists, no preexisting t3r_gate0_* artifacts in g0b_d420, OUT_DIR exists, roarm_rl.rerun_contract.validate_rerun_artifact signature (rerun_contract.py:114-130) matches the call's keyword set exactly, and the results JSON serializer needs no default= on the happy path (every field traced to native float/int/bool/str/None).
